verdict.rationale: Reader is a plain HTTP API driven entirely by URLs and request headers, with curl examples. It also ships a prebuilt container image that bundles headless Chrome, so it can be scripted non-interactively or self-hosted inside automation pipelines. However, the evidence never explicitly documents CI usage, so headless operation is shown but in-CI automation is only implied. missing for 10: explicit CI/pipeline integration docs or examples (e.g. GitHub Actions), documented non-interactive auth and rate-limit guidance for automated runs, independent hands-on corroboration of CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: It bundles headless Chrome, LibreOffice, and CJK fonts, so you can run Reader without building it yourself.
It converts any URL to an **LLM-friendly** input with `https://r.jina.ai/https://your.url`.
`x-engine` — enforces a fetching engine: `browser` (headless Chrome), `curl` (lightweight, no JS), or `auto`
